    Sample size per generation NN. Increase the sample size NN will monotonically increase the on manifold fraction ρ\rho.

    • –

      Note this scaling is almost linear, so to get half of the variance on manifold, one need (N+1)​s≈d(N+1)s\approx d. In reality, d∼109d\sim 10^{9} , which makes this impossible.

    • –

      In most realistic regimes N≪dN\ll d, which makes this on manifold ratio per step nearly negligible.

E.4 Quadratic landscape analysis

Proof of Proposition 3.

Consider a quadratic potential centered, i.e. peaked at the origin θ∗=0\theta^{*}=0.

R⁡(θ)=−12​θ⊤​Q​θR(\theta)=-\frac{1}{2}\theta^{\top}Q\theta (60)

At current state θ0\theta_{0}, the reward at perturbed locations with observation noise are, where ξi∼𝒩⁡(0,1)\xi_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1), ϵi∼𝒩⁡(0,Id)\epsilon_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})

Ri\displaystyle R_{i} =R⁡(θ0+σ​ϵi)+σξ​ξi\displaystyle=R(\theta_{0}+\sigma\epsilon_{i})+\sigma_{\xi}\xi_{i}
=−12​(θ0+σ​ϵi)⊤​Q​(θ0+σ​ϵi)+σξ​ξi\displaystyle=-\frac{1}{2}(\theta_{0}+\sigma\epsilon_{i})^{\top}Q(\theta_{0}+\sigma\epsilon_{i})+\sigma_{\xi}\xi_{i}
=−12​θ0⊤​Q​θ0−σ​θ0⊤​Q​ϵi−σ22​ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi+σξ​ξi\displaystyle=-\frac{1}{2}\theta_{0}^{\top}Q\theta_{0}-\sigma\,\theta_{0}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}-\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}+\sigma_{\xi}\xi_{i} (61)

Expectation of reward reads, which is the population mean of reward samples

𝔼⁡[Ri]=−12​θ0⊤​Q​θ0−σ22​Tr​Q\mathbb{E}[R_{i}]=-\frac{1}{2}\theta_{0}^{\top}Q\theta_{0}-\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2}\mathrm{Tr}Q (62)

Center the rewards with population mean, we define

R~i:=Ri−𝔼⁡[Ri]\tilde{R}_{i}:=R_{i}-\mathbb{E}[R_{i}] (63)

Centered reward has three terms, linear AA, quadratic BB, and noise CC

R~i=−σ​θ0⊤​Q​ϵi⏟linear ​A​−σ22​(ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi−Tr​Q)⏟quad ​B+σξ​ξi⏟scalar noise ​C\tilde{R}_{i}=\underbrace{-\sigma\,\theta_{0}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}}_{\text{linear }A}\underbrace{-\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2}(\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}-\mathrm{Tr}Q)}_{\text{quad }B}+\underbrace{\sigma_{\xi}\xi_{i}}_{\text{scalar noise }C} (64)

One can abbreviate 𝐯:=Q⊤​θ0\mathbf{v}:=Q^{\top}\theta_{0} as the negative gradient.

The weight update reads,

Δ​θ\displaystyle\Delta\theta =α⋅1N∑i=1NZiϵi\displaystyle=\alpha\cdot\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}Z_{i}\epsilon_{i}
=αN​σR​∑i=1NR~i​ϵi\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha}{N\sigma_{R}}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i} (65)

Since perturbations R~i​ϵi\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i} are i.i.d. sampled

𝔼⁡[Δ​θ]=ασR​𝔼​[R~i​ϵi]\mathbb{E}[\Delta\theta]=\frac{\alpha}{\sigma_{R}}\mathbb{E}[\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i}] (66)

and

Cov⁡[Δ​θ]=α2N​σR2​Cov​[R~i​ϵi]\mathrm{Cov}[\Delta\theta]=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N\sigma_{R}^{2}}\mathrm{Cov}[\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i}] (67)

One observe that both R~i\tilde{R}_{i} and R~i​ϵi\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i} are polynomial functions of gaussian random variables ϵi\epsilon_{i} and ξi\xi_{i} (up to 3rd order), thus we can compute their moment of any order via Wick-Isserlis theorem (Wick, 1950; Isserlis, 1918), including mean and covariance of them.

Here are the specific calculations:

Reward variance

Note that all three terms A,B,CA,B,C are centered

𝔼⁡[A]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[A] =0\displaystyle=0
𝔼⁡[B]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[B] =0\displaystyle=0
𝔼⁡[C]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[C] =0\displaystyle=0 (68)

Further A⟂CA\perp C, B⟂CB\perp C due to independence of noise, and

𝔼⁡[A​B]=0\mathbb{E}[AB]=0 (69)

as it only has polynomial of ϵi\epsilon_{i} of odd order 1 and 3, thus its expectation is 0. Thus, A,B,CA,B,C are not correlated with one another. Thus,

Var⁡[R~i]\displaystyle\mathrm{Var}[\tilde{R}_{i}] =𝔼⁡[R~i2]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\tilde{R}_{i}^{2}]
=𝔼⁡[A2]+𝔼⁡[B2]+𝔼⁡[C2]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[A^{2}]+\mathbb{E}[B^{2}]+\mathbb{E}[C^{2}] (70)

all cross terms vanish due to no correlation.

𝔼⁡[A2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[A^{2}] =𝔼⁡[(−σ​θ0⊤​Q​ϵi)⋅(−σ​θ0⊤​Q​ϵi)]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[(-\sigma\,\theta_{0}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i})\cdot(-\sigma\,\theta_{0}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i})]
=σ2​θ0⊤​Q​Q⊤​θ0\displaystyle=\sigma^{2}\theta_{0}^{\top}QQ^{\top}\theta_{0}
=σ2​‖𝐯‖2\displaystyle=\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2} (71)
𝔼⁡[C2]=σξ2\mathbb{E}[C^{2}]=\sigma_{\xi}^{2} (72)
𝔼⁡[B2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[B^{2}] =𝔼⁡[(σ22​(ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi−Tr​Q))2]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[(\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2}(\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}-\mathrm{Tr}Q))^{2}]
=σ44​𝔼​[ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi⋅(ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi−Tr​Q)−Tr​Q⋅(ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi−Tr​Q)]\displaystyle=\frac{\sigma^{4}}{4}\mathbb{E}[\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}\cdot(\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}-\mathrm{Tr}Q)-\mathrm{Tr}Q\cdot(\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}-\mathrm{Tr}Q)]
=σ44​(𝔼⁡[ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi⋅ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi]−(Tr​Q)2)\displaystyle=\frac{\sigma^{4}}{4}\Big(\mathbb{E}[\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}\cdot\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}]-(\mathrm{Tr}Q)^{2}\Big) (73)

The first quintic polynomial of ϵi\epsilon_{i} can be tackled by Wick-Isserelis theorem. With slight mis-use of notation, here we let ϵa\epsilon_{a} denote the aath element of ϵi\epsilon_{i} vector.

Then

𝔼⁡[ϵa​ϵb​ϵc​ϵd]=Ia​b​Ic​d+Ia​d​Ib​c+Ia​c​Ib​d\mathbb{E}[\epsilon_{a}\epsilon_{b}\epsilon_{c}\epsilon_{d}]=I_{ab}I_{cd}+I_{ad}I_{bc}+I_{ac}I_{bd} (74)

thus

𝔼⁡[ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi⋅ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}\cdot\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}] =𝔼⁡[∑a,b,c,dQa​b​Qc​d​ϵa​ϵb​ϵc​ϵd]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\sum_{a,b,c,d}Q_{ab}Q_{cd}\epsilon_{a}\epsilon_{b}\epsilon_{c}\epsilon_{d}]
=∑a,b,c,dQa​b​Qc​d​𝔼​[ϵa​ϵb​ϵc​ϵd]\displaystyle=\sum_{a,b,c,d}Q_{ab}Q_{cd}\mathbb{E}[\epsilon_{a}\epsilon_{b}\epsilon_{c}\epsilon_{d}]
=∑a,b,c,dQa​b​Qc​d​(δa​b​δc​d+δa​c​δb​d+δa​d​δb​c)\displaystyle=\sum_{a,b,c,d}Q_{ab}Q_{cd}(\delta_{ab}\delta_{cd}+\delta_{ac}\delta_{bd}+\delta_{ad}\delta_{bc})
=Tr​Q​Tr​Q+Tr⁡[Q⊤​Q]+Tr⁡[Q​Q]\displaystyle=\mathrm{Tr}Q\mathrm{Tr}Q+\mathrm{Tr}[Q^{\top}Q]+\mathrm{Tr}[QQ] (75)

Thus

𝔼⁡[B2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[B^{2}] =σ44​(𝔼⁡[ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi⋅ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi]−(Tr​Q)2)\displaystyle=\frac{\sigma^{4}}{4}\Big(\mathbb{E}[\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}\cdot\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}]-(\mathrm{Tr}Q)^{2}\Big)
=σ44​((Tr​Q)2+2​T​r​[Q2]−(Tr​Q)2)\displaystyle=\frac{\sigma^{4}}{4}\Big((\mathrm{Tr}Q)^{2}+2\mathrm{Tr}[Q^{2}]-(\mathrm{Tr}Q)^{2}\Big)
=σ42​Tr​[Q2]\displaystyle=\frac{\sigma^{4}}{2}\mathrm{Tr}[Q^{2}] (76)

In sum, the population variance of reward reads,

Var⁡[R~i]=σ2​‖𝐯‖2+σ42​Tr​[Q2]+σξ2\mathrm{Var}[\tilde{R}_{i}]=\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{4}}{2}\mathrm{Tr}[Q^{2}]+\sigma_{\xi}^{2} (77)

and the population standard deviation is

σR=σ2​‖𝐯‖2+σ42​Tr​[Q2]+σξ2\sigma_{R}=\sqrt{\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{4}}{2}\mathrm{Tr}[Q^{2}]+\sigma_{\xi}^{2}} (78)

Expectation of parameter update

Next let’s examine expectation of parameter change, where the key is 𝔼⁡[R~i​ϵi]\mathbb{E}[\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i}], decomposing into three terms

𝔼⁡[R~i​ϵi]=𝔼⁡[A​ϵi]+𝔼⁡[B​ϵi]+𝔼⁡[C​ϵi]\mathbb{E}[\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i}]=\mathbb{E}[A\epsilon_{i}]+\mathbb{E}[B\epsilon_{i}]+\mathbb{E}[C\epsilon_{i}] (79)

Second term vanish due to the odd order of Gaussian variable,

𝔼⁡[B​ϵi]=0\mathbb{E}[B\epsilon_{i}]=0 (80)

Third term vanish due to independence ϵi⟂ξi\epsilon_{i}\perp\xi_{i}

𝔼⁡[C​ϵi]=0\mathbb{E}[C\epsilon_{i}]=0 (81)

First term is easy to calculate

𝔼⁡[A​ϵi]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[A\epsilon_{i}] =𝔼⁡[(−σ​θ0⊤​Q​ϵi)​ϵi]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[(-\sigma\,\theta_{0}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i})\epsilon_{i}]
=−σ​𝔼​[ϵi​(ϵi⊤​𝐯)]\displaystyle=-\sigma\mathbb{E}[\epsilon_{i}(\epsilon_{i}^{\top}\mathbf{v})]
=−σ​𝐯\displaystyle=-\sigma\mathbf{v} (82)

So in sum,

𝔼⁡[R~i​ϵi]=−σ​𝐯\mathbb{E}[\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i}]=-\sigma\mathbf{v} (83)
𝔼⁡[Δ​θ]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\Delta\theta] =ασR​𝔼​[R~i​ϵi]\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha}{\sigma_{R}}\mathbb{E}[\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i}]
=−α​σ​𝐯σR\displaystyle=\frac{-\alpha\sigma\mathbf{v}}{\sigma_{R}}
=−α​σ​𝐯σ2​‖𝐯‖2+σ42​Tr​[Q2]+σξ2\displaystyle=\frac{-\alpha\sigma\mathbf{v}}{\sqrt{\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{4}}{2}\mathrm{Tr}[Q^{2}]+\sigma_{\xi}^{2}}} (84)

which is on expectation aligned with local gradient direction, but scaled by signal to noise ratio.

Variance of parameter update

Finally, let’s examine variance of parameter change, where the key is Cov⁡[R~i​ϵi]\mathrm{Cov}[\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i}],

Cov⁡[R~i​ϵi]\displaystyle\mathrm{Cov}[\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i}] =𝔼⁡[R~i​ϵi​(R~i​ϵi)⊤]−𝔼⁡[R~i​ϵi]​𝔼​[R~i​ϵi]⊤\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i}(\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i})^{\top}]-\mathbb{E}[\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i}]\mathbb{E}[\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i}]^{\top}
=𝔼⁡[R~i2​ϵi​ϵi⊤]−σ2​𝐯𝐯⊤\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\tilde{R}_{i}^{2}\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]-\sigma^{2}\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}^{\top} (85)

Tackling the first term, using the same logic (odd order and independence) to eliminate terms,

𝔼⁡[R~i2​ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\tilde{R}_{i}^{2}\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}] =𝔼⁡[(A+B+C)2​ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[(A+B+C)^{2}\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]
=𝔼⁡[(A2+B2+C2+2​A​B+2​B​C+2​A​C)​ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[(A^{2}+B^{2}+C^{2}+2AB+2BC+2AC)\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]
=𝔼⁡[(A2+B2+C2)​ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[(A^{2}+B^{2}+C^{2})\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}] (86)

Tackle CC term.

𝔼⁡[C2​ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[C^{2}\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}] =𝔼⁡[C2]​𝔼​[ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[C^{2}]\mathbb{E}[\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]
=σξ2​Id\displaystyle=\sigma_{\xi}^{2}I_{d} (87)

Tackle AA term

𝔼⁡[A2​ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[A^{2}\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}] =𝔼⁡[(−σ​θ0⊤​Q​ϵi)2​ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[(-\sigma\,\theta_{0}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i})^{2}\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]
=σ2​𝔼​[(𝐯⊤​ϵi)2​ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle=\sigma^{2}\mathbb{E}[(\mathbf{v}^{\top}\epsilon_{i})^{2}\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}] (88)

using the same Wick theorem trick we have each element

𝔼​[(𝐯⊤​ϵi)2​ϵi​ϵi⊤]c​d\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[(\mathbf{v}^{\top}\epsilon_{i})^{2}\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]_{cd} =𝔼⁡[∑a,b𝐯a​𝐯b​ϵa​ϵb​ϵc​ϵd]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\sum_{a,b}\mathbf{v}_{a}\mathbf{v}_{b}\epsilon_{a}\epsilon_{b}\epsilon_{c}\epsilon_{d}]
=∑a,b𝐯a​𝐯b​𝔼​[ϵa​ϵb​ϵc​ϵd]\displaystyle=\sum_{a,b}\mathbf{v}_{a}\mathbf{v}_{b}\mathbb{E}[\epsilon_{a}\epsilon_{b}\epsilon_{c}\epsilon_{d}]
=∑a,b𝐯a​𝐯b​(δa​b​δc​d+δa​c​δb​d+δa​d​δc​b)\displaystyle=\sum_{a,b}\mathbf{v}_{a}\mathbf{v}_{b}(\delta_{ab}\delta_{cd}+\delta_{ac}\delta_{bd}+\delta_{ad}\delta_{cb})
=‖𝐯‖2​δc​d+𝐯c​𝐯d+𝐯d​𝐯c\displaystyle=\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}\delta_{cd}+\mathbf{v}_{c}\mathbf{v}_{d}+\mathbf{v}_{d}\mathbf{v}_{c} (89)

Thus,

𝔼⁡[A2​ϵi​ϵi⊤]=σ2​(‖𝐯‖2​Id+2​𝐯𝐯⊤)\mathbb{E}[A^{2}\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]=\sigma^{2}(\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}I_{d}+2\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}^{\top}) (90)

Finally, tackle BB term

𝔼⁡[B2​ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[B^{2}\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}] =𝔼⁡[(σ22​(ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi−Tr​Q))2​ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[(\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2}(\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}-\mathrm{Tr}Q))^{2}\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]
=σ44​𝔼​[((ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi)2−2​T​r​Q⋅ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi+(Tr​Q)2)​ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle=\frac{\sigma^{4}}{4}\mathbb{E}[\Big((\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i})^{2}-2\mathrm{Tr}Q\cdot\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}+(\mathrm{Tr}Q)^{2}\Big)\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}] (91)

where we encounter 2nd, 4th and 6th order terms.

2nd order term

𝔼⁡[(Tr​Q)2​ϵi​ϵi⊤]=(Tr​Q)2​Id\mathbb{E}[(\mathrm{Tr}Q)^{2}\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]=(\mathrm{Tr}Q)^{2}I_{d} (92)

4th order term

𝔼​[ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi⋅ϵi​ϵi⊤]c​d\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}\cdot\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]_{cd} =𝔼⁡[∑a,bQa​b​ϵa​ϵb​ϵc​ϵd]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\sum_{a,b}Q_{ab}\epsilon_{a}\epsilon_{b}\epsilon_{c}\epsilon_{d}]
=∑a,bQa​b​(δa​b​δc​d+δa​c​δb​d+δa​d​δc​b)\displaystyle=\sum_{a,b}Q_{ab}(\delta_{ab}\delta_{cd}+\delta_{ac}\delta_{bd}+\delta_{ad}\delta_{cb})
=Tr​Q⋅δc​d+Qc​d+Qd​c\displaystyle=\mathrm{Tr}Q\cdot\delta_{cd}+Q_{cd}+Q_{dc} (93)

Thus

𝔼⁡[ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi⋅ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}\cdot\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}] =Tr​Q⋅Id+Q+Q⊤\displaystyle=\mathrm{Tr}Q\cdot I_{d}+Q+Q^{\top}
=Tr​Q⋅Id+2​Q\displaystyle=\mathrm{Tr}Q\cdot I_{d}+2Q (94)

6th order term

𝔼​[((ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi)2)​ϵi​ϵi⊤]e​f=𝔼⁡[∑a,b,c,dQa​b​Qc​d​ϵa​ϵb​ϵc​ϵd​ϵe​ϵf]\mathbb{E}[\Big((\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i})^{2}\Big)\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]_{ef}=\mathbb{E}[\sum_{a,b,c,d}Q_{ab}Q_{cd}\epsilon_{a}\epsilon_{b}\epsilon_{c}\epsilon_{d}\epsilon_{e}\epsilon_{f}] (95)

Note this has C62=15C_{6}^{2}=15 pairings, with some diagrammatic reasoning, we can find topologically we have three types

𝔼​[((ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi)2)​ϵi​ϵi⊤]e​f\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\Big((\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i})^{2}\Big)\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]_{ef} =𝔼⁡[∑a,b,c,dQa​b​Qc​d​ϵa​ϵb​ϵc​ϵd​ϵe​ϵf]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\sum_{a,b,c,d}Q_{ab}Q_{cd}\epsilon_{a}\epsilon_{b}\epsilon_{c}\epsilon_{d}\epsilon_{e}\epsilon_{f}]
=∑a,b,c,dQa​b​Qc​d​(δa​b​δc​d​δe​f⏟1​case+δa​c​δb​d​δe​f+…⏟2​case+CLOSE\displaystyle=\sum_{a,b,c,d}Q_{ab}Q_{cd}\Big(\underbrace{\delta_{ab}\delta_{cd}\delta_{ef}}_{1\text{case}}+\underbrace{\delta_{ac}\delta_{bd}\delta_{ef}+...}_{2\text{case}}+
OPENδa​e​δb​f​δc​d+…⏟4​case+δa​e​δc​f​δb​d+…⏟8​case)\displaystyle\quad\quad\underbrace{\delta_{ae}\delta_{bf}\delta_{cd}+...}_{4\text{case}}+\underbrace{\delta_{ae}\delta_{cf}\delta_{bd}+...}_{8\text{case}}\Big)
=((Tr​Q)2+2​T​r​Q2)​δe​f+4​T​r​Q⋅Qe​f+8​[Q2]e​f\displaystyle=((\mathrm{Tr}Q)^{2}+2\mathrm{Tr}Q^{2})\delta_{ef}+4\mathrm{Tr}Q\cdot Q_{ef}+8[Q^{2}]_{ef} (96)

Thus

𝔼⁡[((ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi)2)​ϵi​ϵi⊤]=((Tr​Q)2+2​Tr​Q2)​Id+4​Tr​Q⋅Q+8​Q2\mathbb{E}[\Big((\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i})^{2}\Big)\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]=((\mathrm{Tr}Q)^{2}+2\mathrm{Tr}Q^{2})I_{d}+4\mathrm{Tr}Q\cdot Q+8Q^{2} (97)

In summary

𝔼⁡[B2​ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[B^{2}\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}] =σ44​𝔼​[((ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi)2−2​T​r​Q⋅ϵi⊤​Q​ϵi+(Tr​Q)2)​ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle=\frac{\sigma^{4}}{4}\mathbb{E}[\Big((\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i})^{2}-2\mathrm{Tr}Q\cdot\epsilon_{i}^{\top}Q\epsilon_{i}+(\mathrm{Tr}Q)^{2}\Big)\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]
=σ44[((TrQ)2+2TrQ2)Id+4TrQ⋅Q+8Q2\displaystyle=\frac{\sigma^{4}}{4}\Big[((\mathrm{Tr}Q)^{2}+2\mathrm{Tr}Q^{2})I_{d}+4\mathrm{Tr}Q\cdot Q+8Q^{2}
−2TrQ⋅(TrQ⋅Id+2Q)\displaystyle\quad-2\mathrm{Tr}Q\cdot(\mathrm{Tr}Q\cdot I_{d}+2Q)
+(TrQ)2Id]\displaystyle\quad+(\mathrm{Tr}Q)^{2}I_{d}\Big]
=σ44​[(2​T​r​Q2)​Id+8​Q2]\displaystyle=\frac{\sigma^{4}}{4}\Big[(2\mathrm{Tr}Q^{2})I_{d}+8Q^{2}\Big]
=σ42​[(Tr​Q2)⋅Id+4​Q2]\displaystyle=\frac{\sigma^{4}}{2}\Big[(\mathrm{Tr}Q^{2})\cdot I_{d}+4Q^{2}\Big] (98)

Thus

𝔼⁡[R~i2​ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\tilde{R}_{i}^{2}\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}] =𝔼⁡[(A2+B2+C2)​ϵi​ϵi⊤]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[(A^{2}+B^{2}+C^{2})\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]
=σ2​(‖𝐯‖2​Id+2​𝐯𝐯⊤)+σ42​[(Tr​Q2)⋅Id+4​Q2]+σξ2​Id\displaystyle=\sigma^{2}(\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}I_{d}+2\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}^{\top})+\frac{\sigma^{4}}{2}\Big[(\mathrm{Tr}Q^{2})\cdot I_{d}+4Q^{2}\Big]+\sigma_{\xi}^{2}I_{d} (99)

The covariance term reads

Cov⁡[R~i​ϵi]\displaystyle\mathrm{Cov}[\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i}] =𝔼⁡[R~i2​ϵi​ϵi⊤]−σ2​𝐯𝐯⊤\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\tilde{R}_{i}^{2}\epsilon_{i}\epsilon_{i}^{\top}]-\sigma^{2}\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}^{\top}
=σ2​(‖𝐯‖2​Id+𝐯𝐯⊤)+σ42​[(Tr​Q2)⋅Id+4​Q2]+σξ2​Id\displaystyle=\sigma^{2}(\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}I_{d}+\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}^{\top})+\frac{\sigma^{4}}{2}\Big[(\mathrm{Tr}Q^{2})\cdot I_{d}+4Q^{2}\Big]+\sigma_{\xi}^{2}I_{d} (100)

Recall that Var⁡[R~i]=σ2​‖𝐯‖2+σ42​Tr​[Q2]+σξ2\mathrm{Var}[\tilde{R}_{i}]=\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{4}}{2}\mathrm{Tr}[Q^{2}]+\sigma_{\xi}^{2}

Cov⁡[R~i​ϵi]=σ2​𝐯𝐯⊤+2​σ4​Q2+σR2​Id\mathrm{Cov}[\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i}]=\sigma^{2}\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}^{\top}+2\sigma^{4}Q^{2}+\sigma_{R}^{2}I_{d} (101)

Thus in summary we have mean and covariance of parameter update, 𝐯:=Q​θ0\mathbf{v}:=Q\theta_{0}

𝔼⁡[Δ​θ]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\Delta\theta] =ασR​𝔼​[R~i​ϵi]\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha}{\sigma_{R}}\mathbb{E}[\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i}]
=−α​σ​𝐯σR\displaystyle=\frac{-\alpha\sigma\mathbf{v}}{\sigma_{R}} (102)
Cov⁡[Δ​θ]\displaystyle\mathrm{Cov}[\Delta\theta] =α2N​σR2​Cov​[R~i​ϵi]\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N\sigma_{R}^{2}}\mathrm{Cov}[\tilde{R}_{i}\epsilon_{i}]
=α2N​σR2​(σ2​𝐯𝐯⊤+2​σ4​Q2+σR2​Id)\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N\sigma_{R}^{2}}\Big(\sigma^{2}\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}^{\top}+2\sigma^{4}Q^{2}+\sigma_{R}^{2}I_{d}\Big)
=α2N​Id+α2N​σR2​(σ2​𝐯𝐯⊤+2​σ4​Q2)\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}I_{d}+\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N\sigma_{R}^{2}}\Big(\sigma^{2}\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}^{\top}+2\sigma^{4}Q^{2}\Big) (103)

The covariance of weight update has three terms

  • •

    An isotropic variance term from the Gaussian exploration per se. α2N​Id\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}I_{d}

  • •

    A rank-1 term along current gradient direction 𝐯\mathbf{v}, α2​σ2N​σR2​𝐯𝐯⊤\frac{\alpha^{2}\sigma^{2}}{N\sigma_{R}^{2}}\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}^{\top}

  • •

    A term corresponding to landscape curvature, i.e. higher variance along higher curvature directions, 2​σ4​α2N​σR2​Q2\frac{2\sigma^{4}\alpha^{2}}{N\sigma_{R}^{2}}Q^{2}

∎

Order analysis of quadratic landscape

Consider the relative magnitudes of the covariance terms, using the first term as a reference:

  • •

    The second term (aligned with the gradient direction) is of order σ2σR2​‖𝐯‖2\frac{\sigma^{2}}{\sigma_{R}^{2}}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}.

  • •

    The third term (along each direction 𝐮\mathbf{u}) is of order 2​σ4σR2​𝐮⊤​Q2​𝐮\frac{2\sigma^{4}}{\sigma_{R}^{2}}\,\mathbf{u}^{\top}Q^{2}\mathbf{u}.

Since in practice 2​σ22\sigma^{2} is very small (e.g., 4.5×10−64.5\times 10^{-6}), the quadratic term generally acts as a small perturbation. To determine when the third (quadratic) term becomes comparable to the second, compare the terms along a specific direction 𝐮\mathbf{u}:

2​σ4σR2​𝐮⊤​Q2​𝐮\displaystyle\frac{2\sigma^{4}}{\sigma_{R}^{2}}\,\mathbf{u}^{\top}Q^{2}\mathbf{u} ≈σ2σR2​‖𝐯‖2\displaystyle\approx\frac{\sigma^{2}}{\sigma_{R}^{2}}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}
2​σ2​𝐮⊤​Q2​𝐮\displaystyle 2\sigma^{2}\,\mathbf{u}^{\top}Q^{2}\mathbf{u} ≈θ0⊤​Q2​θ0\displaystyle\approx\theta_{0}^{\top}Q^{2}\theta_{0}
𝐮⊤​Q2​𝐮\displaystyle\mathbf{u}^{\top}Q^{2}\mathbf{u} ≈12​σ2​θ0⊤​Q2​θ0\displaystyle\approx\frac{1}{2\sigma^{2}}\,\theta_{0}^{\top}Q^{2}\theta_{0} (104)

Assume 𝐮\mathbf{u} is an eigenvector of QQ with eigenvalue λk\lambda_{k},

λk2\displaystyle\lambda_{k}^{2} ≈12​σ2​θ0⊤​Q2​θ0\displaystyle\approx\frac{1}{2\sigma^{2}}\theta_{0}^{\top}Q^{2}\theta_{0}
λk\displaystyle\lambda_{k} ≈‖𝐯‖2​σ\displaystyle\approx\frac{\|\mathbf{v}\|}{\sqrt{2}\sigma} (105)
λk2≈12​σ2​∑i=1dλi2​(θ0⊤​𝐮i)2\lambda_{k}^{2}\approx\frac{1}{2\sigma^{2}}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\lambda_{i}^{2}(\theta_{0}^{\top}\mathbf{u}_{i})^{2} (106)

This shows that the current gradient norm ‖𝐯‖\|\mathbf{v}\| needs to be much smaller (at least σ\sigma times) and the eigenvalue / curvature of the probe direction needs to be sharp enough for the 3rd term to be comparable to the 2nd term. Two scenarios this could happen

  • •

    For really sharply curved directions λk\lambda_{k} this is usually be true.

  • •

    The current state θ0\theta_{0} is close to optimum θ∗=0\theta^{*}=0 or lies in the vast valley of degenerate solution, i.e. Q​θ0=0Q\theta_{0}=0, θ0\theta_{0} in the null space of QQ.

Manifold Alignment of Update

Define the projections onto the gradient direction 𝐯=Q​θ0\mathbf{v}=Q\theta_{0} and its orthogonal complement:

P∥\displaystyle P^{\parallel} :=𝐯𝐯⊤‖𝐯‖2,P⟂:=Id−P∥.\displaystyle:=\frac{\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}^{\top}}{\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}},\qquad P^{\perp}:=I_{d}-P^{\parallel}. (107)

The on-manifold expected squared norm decomposes as

𝔼​‖P∥​Δ​θ‖2\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\|P^{\parallel}\Delta\theta\|^{2} =‖𝔼⁡[P∥​Δ​θ]‖2+Tr⁡[Cov⁡[P∥​Δ​θ]].\displaystyle=\|\mathbb{E}[P^{\parallel}\Delta\theta]\|^{2}+\mathrm{Tr}[\mathrm{Cov}[P^{\parallel}\Delta\theta]]. (108)

For the first term, since 𝔼⁡[Δ​θ]=−α​σ​𝐯σR\mathbb{E}[\Delta\theta]=\frac{-\alpha\sigma\,\mathbf{v}}{\sigma_{R}} is already along 𝐯\mathbf{v}, we have P∥​𝔼​[Δ​θ]=𝔼⁡[Δ​θ]P^{\parallel}\mathbb{E}[\Delta\theta]=\mathbb{E}[\Delta\theta], so

‖𝔼⁡[P∥​Δ​θ]‖2\displaystyle\|\mathbb{E}[P^{\parallel}\Delta\theta]\|^{2} =‖𝔼⁡[Δ​θ]‖2=α2​σ2​‖𝐯‖2σR2.\displaystyle=\|\mathbb{E}[\Delta\theta]\|^{2}=\frac{\alpha^{2}\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}}{\sigma_{R}^{2}}. (109)

For the second term, we project the covariance (14) onto P∥P^{\parallel}:

Cov⁡[P∥​Δ​θ]\displaystyle\mathrm{Cov}[P^{\parallel}\Delta\theta] =P∥​Cov​[Δ​θ]​P∥\displaystyle=P^{\parallel}\,\mathrm{Cov}[\Delta\theta]\,P^{\parallel}
=α2N​σR2​P∥​(σ2​𝐯𝐯⊤+2​σ4​Q2+σR2​Id)​P∥.\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N\sigma_{R}^{2}}P^{\parallel}\left(\sigma^{2}\,\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}^{\top}+2\sigma^{4}Q^{2}+\sigma_{R}^{2}\,I_{d}\right)P^{\parallel}. (110)

Evaluating each term using P∥​𝐯𝐯⊤​P∥=‖𝐯‖2​P∥P^{\parallel}\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}^{\top}P^{\parallel}=\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}P^{\parallel}, P∥​Q2​P∥=(𝐯^⊤​Q2​𝐯^)​P∥P^{\parallel}Q^{2}P^{\parallel}=(\hat{\mathbf{v}}^{\top}Q^{2}\hat{\mathbf{v}})\,P^{\parallel} where 𝐯^:=𝐯/‖𝐯‖\hat{\mathbf{v}}:=\mathbf{v}/\|\mathbf{v}\|, and P∥​Id​P∥=P∥P^{\parallel}I_{d}\,P^{\parallel}=P^{\parallel}:

Cov⁡[P∥​Δ​θ]\displaystyle\mathrm{Cov}[P^{\parallel}\Delta\theta] =α2N​σR2​(σ2​‖𝐯‖2+2​σ4​𝐯^⊤​Q2​𝐯^+σR2)​P∥.\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N\sigma_{R}^{2}}\left(\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}+2\sigma^{4}\,\hat{\mathbf{v}}^{\top}Q^{2}\hat{\mathbf{v}}+\sigma_{R}^{2}\right)P^{\parallel}. (111)

Taking the trace (Tr⁡[P∥]=1\mathrm{Tr}[P^{\parallel}]=1) and combining:

𝔼​‖P∥​Δ​θ‖2\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\|P^{\parallel}\Delta\theta\|^{2} =α2​σ2​‖𝐯‖2σR2+α2N​σR2​(σ2​‖𝐯‖2+2​σ4​𝐯^⊤​Q2​𝐯^+σR2).\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha^{2}\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}}{\sigma_{R}^{2}}+\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N\sigma_{R}^{2}}\left(\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}+2\sigma^{4}\,\hat{\mathbf{v}}^{\top}Q^{2}\hat{\mathbf{v}}+\sigma_{R}^{2}\right). (112)

The total expected squared norm follows analogously using Tr⁡[𝐯𝐯⊤]=‖𝐯‖2\mathrm{Tr}[\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}^{\top}]=\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}, Tr⁡[Q2]=Tr⁡[Q2]\mathrm{Tr}[Q^{2}]=\mathrm{Tr}[Q^{2}], and Tr⁡[Id]=d\mathrm{Tr}[I_{d}]=d:

𝔼​‖Δ​θ‖2\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\|\Delta\theta\|^{2} =α2​σ2​‖𝐯‖2σR2+α2N​σR2​(σ2​‖𝐯‖2+2​σ4​Tr​[Q2]+d​σR2).\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha^{2}\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}}{\sigma_{R}^{2}}+\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N\sigma_{R}^{2}}\left(\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}+2\sigma^{4}\,\mathrm{Tr}[Q^{2}]+d\,\sigma_{R}^{2}\right). (113)

Factoring out α2/(N​σR2)\alpha^{2}/(N\sigma_{R}^{2}) from both expressions — noting that the mean-squared term α2​σ2​‖𝐯‖2σR2\frac{\alpha^{2}\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}}{\sigma_{R}^{2}} contributes N​σ2​‖𝐯‖2N\,\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2} after extracting the common factor, which combines with the variance contribution to yield (N+1)​σ2​‖𝐯‖2(N+1)\,\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2} — the on-manifold fraction is

ρ:=𝔼​‖P∥​Δ​θ‖2𝔼​‖Δ​θ‖2=(N+1)​σ2​‖𝐯‖2+2​σ4​𝐯^⊤​Q2​𝐯^+σR2(N+1)​σ2​‖𝐯‖2+2​σ4​Tr​[Q2]+d​σR2.\displaystyle\rho:=\frac{\mathbb{E}\|P^{\parallel}\Delta\theta\|^{2}}{\mathbb{E}\|\Delta\theta\|^{2}}=\frac{(N+1)\,\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}+2\sigma^{4}\,\hat{\mathbf{v}}^{\top}Q^{2}\hat{\mathbf{v}}+\sigma_{R}^{2}}{(N+1)\,\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}+2\sigma^{4}\,\mathrm{Tr}[Q^{2}]+d\,\sigma_{R}^{2}}. (114)

Setting Q2=0Q^{2}=0 and σR2=σ2​‖𝐯‖2+σξ2\sigma_{R}^{2}=\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}+\sigma_{\xi}^{2} recovers the linear-landscape ratio ρ=(1+(N+1)​s)/(d+(N+1)​s)\rho=(1+(N+1)s)/(d+(N+1)s) with s=σ2​‖𝐯‖2/σR2s=\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}/\sigma_{R}^{2}.

E.5 Multi-step ES analysis for quadratic landscape

We could write down the ES iteration as

θ1−θ0\displaystyle\theta_{1}-\theta_{0} =−α​σ​𝐯σR+η0\displaystyle=\frac{-\alpha\sigma\mathbf{v}}{\sigma_{R}}+\eta_{0}
=−α​σσR​Q​θ0+η0\displaystyle=-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}Q\theta_{0}+\eta_{0} (115)

Thus

θt+1=(I−α​σσR​Q)​θt+ηt\theta_{t+1}=\Big(I-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}Q\Big)\ \theta_{t}+\eta_{t} (116)

where,

Cov⁡[ηt]\displaystyle\mathrm{Cov}[\eta_{t}] =α2N​σR2​(σ2​𝐯𝐯⊤+2​σ4​Q2+σR2​Id)\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N\sigma_{R}^{2}}\Big(\sigma^{2}\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}^{\top}+2\sigma^{4}Q^{2}+\sigma_{R}^{2}I_{d}\Big)
=α2N​Id+α2N​σR2​(σ2​Q​θt​θt⊤​Q+2​σ4​Q2)\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}I_{d}+\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N\sigma_{R}^{2}}\Big(\sigma^{2}Q\theta_{t}\theta_{t}^{\top}Q+2\sigma^{4}Q^{2}\Big) (117)

and

σR\displaystyle\sigma_{R} =σ2​‖𝐯‖2+σ42​Tr​[Q2]+σξ2\displaystyle=\sqrt{\sigma^{2}\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{4}}{2}\mathrm{Tr}[Q^{2}]+\sigma_{\xi}^{2}}
=σ2​θt⊤​Q2​θt+σ42​Tr​[Q2]+σξ2\displaystyle=\sqrt{\sigma^{2}\theta_{t}^{\top}Q^{2}\theta_{t}+\frac{\sigma^{4}}{2}\mathrm{Tr}[Q^{2}]+\sigma_{\xi}^{2}} (118)

Simplified ES-optimization process

Consider the simplified ES optimization, where we assume the σR\sigma_{R} is held constant. To simplify it even more, assume ηt\eta_{t} is Gaussian and isotropic each step α2N​Id\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}I_{d}, i.e. ignore the 2nd and 3rd term α2N​σR2​(σ2​Q​θt​θt⊤​Q+2​σ4​Q2)\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N\sigma_{R}^{2}}\Big(\sigma^{2}Q\theta_{t}\theta_{t}^{\top}Q+2\sigma^{4}Q^{2}\Big)

Thus the optimization iteration reads,

θt+1=(I−α​σσR​Q)​θt+ηt,ηt∼𝒩⁡(0,α2N​Id)\theta_{t+1}=\Big(I-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}Q\Big)\theta_{t}+\eta_{t},\quad\eta_{t}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}I_{d}) (119)

This process is known as vector autoregression VAR(1) or discrete-time OU process.

Proof of Proposition 4.

We can write down the generative process of θT\theta_{T} recursively.

θt\displaystyle\theta_{t} =H​θt−1+ηt−1\displaystyle=H\theta_{t-1}+\eta_{t-1}
=H⁡(H​θt−2+ηt−2)+ηt−1\displaystyle=H(H\theta_{t-2}+\eta_{t-2})+\eta_{t-1}
=H2​θt−2+H​ηt−2+ηt−1\displaystyle=H^{2}\theta_{t-2}+H\eta_{t-2}+\eta_{t-1}
=H3​θt−3+H2​ηt−3+H​ηt−2+ηt−1\displaystyle=H^{3}\theta_{t-3}+H^{2}\eta_{t-3}+H\eta_{t-2}+\eta_{t-1}
=Ht​θ0+∑i=1tHi−1​ηt−i\displaystyle=H^{t}\theta_{0}+\sum_{i=1}^{t}H^{i-1}\eta_{t-i} (120)

Note let 𝐮k,λk\mathbf{u}_{k},\lambda_{k} be the eigenvector and eigenvalue of QQ, then

H\displaystyle H =I−α​σσR​Q\displaystyle=I-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}Q
=∑k=1d(1−α​σσR​λk)​𝐮k​𝐮k⊤\displaystyle=\sum_{k=1}^{d}(1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k})\mathbf{u}_{k}\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top} (121)

In this simplification, the distribution comes from the independent Gaussian random vectors {ηi}\{\eta_{i}\}, thus it’s still Gaussian distributed.

Thus we can write down the expectation, which only depends on the first term.

𝔼⁡[θt]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\theta_{t}] =Ht​θ0\displaystyle=H^{t}\theta_{0}
=∑k=1d(1−α​σσR​λk)t​𝐮k​𝐮k⊤​θ0\displaystyle=\sum_{k=1}^{d}(1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k})^{t}\mathbf{u}_{k}\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{0} (122)

Asymptotically,

limt→∞𝔼⁡[θt]\displaystyle\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathbb{E}[\theta_{t}] =limt→∞Ht​θ0\displaystyle=\lim_{t\to\infty}H^{t}\theta_{0}
=limt→∞∑k=1d(1−α​σσR​λk)t​𝐮k​𝐮k⊤​θ0\displaystyle=\lim_{t\to\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{d}(1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k})^{t}\mathbf{u}_{k}\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{0} (123)
  • •

    For flat dimensions λk=0\lambda_{k}=0, then limt→∞(1−α​σσR​λk)t=1\lim_{t\to\infty}(1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k})^{t}=1, thus on expectation the solution won’t move on that direction limt→∞𝔼⁡[𝐮k⊤​θt]=𝐮k⊤​θ0\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{t}]=\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{0}

  • •

    If |1−α​σσR​λk|>1|1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k}|>1, this will diverge to infinity. limt→∞𝔼⁡[𝐮k⊤​θt]=∞\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{t}]=\infty

    • –

      Specifically, when λk<0\lambda_{k}<0 concave dimensions

    • –

      or for α​σσR​λk>2\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k}>2, this will diverge. This could happen for very sharply curved directions where curvature exceeds λk>2​σRα​σ\lambda_{k}>2\frac{\sigma_{R}}{\alpha\sigma}. Note for gradient descent this could also be caused by too high learning rate, but here α=σ/2\alpha=\sigma/2.

The covariance depends on the summation ∑i=1tHi−1​ηt−i\sum_{i=1}^{t}H^{i-1}\eta_{t-i}, using the i.i.d. property of the noise {ηi}\{\eta_{i}\} and the Gaussian distribution of noise,

Cov⁡[θt]\displaystyle\mathrm{Cov}[\theta_{t}] =Cov⁡[∑i=1tHi−1​ηt−i]\displaystyle=\mathrm{Cov}[\sum_{i=1}^{t}H^{i-1}\eta_{t-i}]
=∑i=1tCov⁡[Hi−1​ηt−i]\displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{t}\mathrm{Cov}[H^{i-1}\eta_{t-i}]
=∑i=1t(Hi−1)​Cov​[ηt−i]​(Hi−1)⊤\displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{t}(H^{i-1})\mathrm{Cov}[\eta_{t-i}](H^{i-1})^{\top}
=∑i=1t(Hi−1)2​α2N​Id\displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{t}(H^{i-1})^{2}\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}I_{d}
=α2N​∑i=0t−1H2​i\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}H^{2i} (124)

Thus the variance along one eigen axis is the sum of this series.

Cov⁡[𝐮k⊤​θt]\displaystyle\mathrm{Cov}[\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{t}] =α2N​𝐮k⊤​∑i=0t−1H2​i​𝐮k\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}H^{2i}\mathbf{u}_{k}
=α2N​∑i=0t−1(1−α​σσR​λk)2​i\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}(1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k})^{2i} (125)

Using the formula for finite term sum of geometric series,

∑k=0t−1xk={1−xt1−x,x≠1,t,x=1.\sum_{k=0}^{t-1}x^{k}=\begin{cases}\dfrac{1-x^{t}}{1-x},&x\neq 1,\\[6.0pt] t,&x=1.\end{cases} (126)

note that for finite terms this identity holds for |x|>1|x|>1.

The key quantity here is γ2:=(1−α​σσR​λk)2\gamma^{2}:=(1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k})^{2} and its relation to 11. (1−α​σσR​λk)2=1(1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k})^{2}=1 entails λk=0\lambda_{k}=0 or λk=2​σRα​σ\lambda_{k}=\frac{2\sigma_{R}}{\alpha\sigma}Thus, along an eigen direction, the variance reads,

Cov⁡[𝐮k⊤​θt]=α2N​{1−(1−α​σσR​λk)2​t1−(1−α​σσR​λk)2,otherwiset,λk∈{0,2​σRα​σ}\mathrm{Cov}[\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{t}]=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}\begin{cases}\frac{1-(1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k})^{2t}}{1-(1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k})^{2}},&\text{otherwise}\\[6.0pt] t,&\lambda_{k}\in\{0,\frac{2\sigma_{R}}{\alpha\sigma}\}\end{cases} (127)
Cov⁡[𝐮k⊤​θt]=α2N​{1−γ2​t1−γ2,otherwiset,γ2=0,i.e. ​λk∈{0,2​σRα​σ}\mathrm{Cov}[\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{t}]=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}\begin{cases}\frac{1-\gamma^{2t}}{1-\gamma^{2}},&\text{otherwise}\\[6.0pt] t,&\gamma^{2}=0,\text{i.e. }\lambda_{k}\in\{0,\frac{2\sigma_{R}}{\alpha\sigma}\}\end{cases} (128)

∎

Asymptotic behavior

  • •

    In the flat direction, λk=0\lambda_{k}=0, then Cov⁡[𝐮k⊤​θt]=α2N​t\mathrm{Cov}[\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{t}]=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}t, recovering the linear scaling of random walk. Similarly for λk=2​σRα​σ\lambda_{k}=\frac{2\sigma_{R}}{\alpha\sigma}, it increase linearly.

  • •

    In the concave directions, i.e.λk<0\lambda_{k}<0, (1−α​σσR​λk)2>1(1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k})^{2}>1, then this series will diverge towards infinity. limt→∞Cov⁡[𝐮k⊤​θt]=∞\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathrm{Cov}[\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{t}]=\infty

  • •

    For λk≥2​σRα​σ\lambda_{k}\geq\frac{2\sigma_{R}}{\alpha\sigma}, convex direction with too high curvature, then |1−α​σσR​λk|≥1|1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k}|\geq 1, then this series will diverge limt→∞Cov⁡[𝐮k⊤​θt]=∞\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathrm{Cov}[\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{t}]=\infty.

  • •

    For 0<λk<2​σRα​σ0<\lambda_{k}<\frac{2\sigma_{R}}{\alpha\sigma}, then |1−α​σσR​λk|<1|1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k}|<1, then this series will converge, this is the desirable case for optimization. Asymptotically,

    limt→∞Cov⁡[𝐮k⊤​θt]\displaystyle\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathrm{Cov}[\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{t}] =α2N​11−(1−α​σσR​λk)2\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}\frac{1}{1-(1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k})^{2}}
    =α2N​11−γ2\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}\frac{1}{1-\gamma^{2}} (129)
    • –

      The convergence speed is inversely proportional to γ2:=(1−α​σσR​λk)2\gamma^{2}:=(1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k})^{2}. When γ2\gamma^{2} close to 00, the series γ2​t\gamma^{2t} converges faster; when γ2∼1\gamma^{2}\sim 1, the convergence time gets longer and longer.

    • –

      Convergence timescale can be computed 1−γ2​τ=1/21-\gamma^{2\tau}=1/2, then log⁡12=τ​log⁡γ2\log\frac{1}{2}=\tau\log\gamma^{2}, τ=−log⁡2log⁡γ2=−log⁡2log⁡(1−α​σσR​λk)2\tau=-\frac{\log 2}{\log\gamma^{2}}=-\frac{\log 2}{\log(1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k})^{2}} is the characteristic time scale.

    • –

      The converged level is also controlled by γ2\gamma^{2}, specifically α2N​11−γ2\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}\frac{1}{1-\gamma^{2}}. When γ2\gamma^{2} close to 00, converged level is lower; when γ2∼1\gamma^{2}\sim 1 the converged level grow towards infinity

    • –

      Thus directions where λk∼σRα​σ\lambda_{k}\sim\frac{\sigma_{R}}{\alpha\sigma} converge the fastest and the variance are the tightest limt→∞Cov⁡[𝐮k⊤​θt]∼α2N\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathrm{Cov}[\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{t}]\sim\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}. Showing that these directions are the most well controlled by the landscape asymptotically. Specifically when λk=σRα​σ\lambda_{k}=\frac{\sigma_{R}}{\alpha\sigma}, then this direction converges in one iteration H​θ0H\theta_{0}.

E.6 Gradient ascent on quadratic landscape

For comparison with the ES dynamics of Section E.5, we analyze standard (noiseless) gradient ascent44 4 Since we are maximizing the reward, it’s gradient ascent, but still we call it GD for simplicity on the same quadratic landscape R⁡(θ)=−12​θ⊤​Q​θR(\theta)=-\frac{1}{2}\theta^{\top}Q\theta.

The negative gradient at θt\theta_{t} is −∇R​(θt)=Q​θt=𝐯t-\nabla R(\theta_{t})=Q\theta_{t}=\mathbf{v}_{t}. Gradient ascent with learning rate β\beta updates as

θt+1=θt+β∇R(θt)=θt−βQθt=(I−βQ)θt.\theta_{t+1}=\theta_{t}+\beta\nabla R(\theta_{t})=\theta_{t}-\beta\,Q\theta_{t}=(I-\beta Q)\,\theta_{t}. (130)

Define HGD:=I−β​QH_{\mathrm{GD}}:=I-\beta Q, with eigendecomposition

HGD=∑k=1d(1−β​λk)​𝐮k​𝐮k⊤,H_{\mathrm{GD}}=\sum_{k=1}^{d}(1-\beta\lambda_{k})\,\mathbf{u}_{k}\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}, (131)

where λk\lambda_{k} and 𝐮k\mathbf{u}_{k} are the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of QQ. Let γkGD:=1−β​λk\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{GD}}:=1-\beta\lambda_{k} denote the contraction factor along eigendirection 𝐮k\mathbf{u}_{k}.

Trajectory

Since the iteration is deterministic, recursion gives

θt=HGDt​θ0=∑k=1d(γkGD)t​(𝐮k⊤​θ0)​𝐮k.\theta_{t}=H_{\mathrm{GD}}^{t}\,\theta_{0}=\sum_{k=1}^{d}(\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{GD}})^{t}\,(\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{0})\,\mathbf{u}_{k}. (132)

Each eigendirection evolves independently:

𝐮k⊤​θt=(1−β​λk)t​𝐮k⊤​θ0.\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{t}=(1-\beta\lambda_{k})^{t}\,\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{0}. (133)

The squared distance to the optimum θ∗=0\theta^{*}=0 is

‖θt‖2=∑k=1d(1−β​λk)2​t​(𝐮k⊤​θ0)2.\|\theta_{t}\|^{2}=\sum_{k=1}^{d}(1-\beta\lambda_{k})^{2t}\,(\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{0})^{2}. (134)

Convergence conditions

Direction 𝐮k\mathbf{u}_{k} converges if and only if |γkGD|<1|\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{GD}}|<1, i.e.,

0<λk<2β.0<\lambda_{k}<\frac{2}{\beta}. (135)

The three non-convergent modes mirror those of the ES dynamics:

  • •

    Flat directions (λk=0\lambda_{k}=0): γkGD=1\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{GD}}=1, so 𝐮k⊤​θt=𝐮k⊤​θ0\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{t}=\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{0} for all tt, i.e. along flat directions, the gradient ascent freezes at the initial projection.

    This is dramatically different from ES, where along flat directions, the iterate undergoes unbounded diffusion with variance growing as α2​tN\frac{\alpha^{2}t}{N}.

  • •

    Concave directions (λk<0\lambda_{k}<0): γkGD>1\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{GD}}>1, causing exponential divergence |𝐮k⊤​θt|→∞|\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{t}|\to\infty.

  • •

    Overly sharp convex directions (λk≥2/β\lambda_{k}\geq 2/\beta): |γkGD|≥1|\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{GD}}|\geq 1, and the iterate overshoots, oscillating with growing (or non-decaying) amplitude. This explosion can happen due to too large learning rate, or due to too high landscape curvature.

Convergence rate

Within the stable regime 0<λk<2/β0<\lambda_{k}<2/\beta, the convergence timescale along 𝐮k\mathbf{u}_{k} is

τkGD=−log⁡2log⁡(γkGD)2=−log⁡22​log⁡|1−β​λk|.\tau_{k}^{\mathrm{GD}}=\frac{-\log 2}{\log(\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{GD}})^{2}}=\frac{-\log 2}{2\log|1-\beta\lambda_{k}|}. (136)

The optimal eigenvalue is λk=1/β\lambda_{k}=1/\beta, which achieves γkGD=0\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{GD}}=0 and convergence in a single iteration (τkGD=0\tau_{k}^{\mathrm{GD}}=0, since 𝐮k⊤​θ1=0\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{1}=0 exactly). The overall convergence rate is governed by the slowest direction,

τmaxGD=maxk:λk>0−log⁡22​log⁡|1−β​λk|,\tau_{\max}^{\mathrm{GD}}=\max_{k:\,\lambda_{k}>0}\;\frac{-\log 2}{2\log|1-\beta\lambda_{k}|}, (137)

which for small learning rate β​λk≪1\beta\lambda_{k}\ll 1 gives τkGD≈12​β​λk\tau_{k}^{\mathrm{GD}}\approx\frac{1}{2\beta\lambda_{k}}, inversely proportional to the curvature. The condition number κ:=λmax/λmin\kappa:=\lambda_{\max}/\lambda_{\min} (over positive eigenvalues) then controls the ratio of fastest to slowest timescales.

Comparison with ES dynamics

The simplified ES iteration (Proposition 4) takes the form

θt+1=HES​θt+ηt,HES=I−α​σσR​Q,\theta_{t+1}=H_{\mathrm{ES}}\,\theta_{t}+\eta_{t},\qquad H_{\mathrm{ES}}=I-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}Q, (138)

with γkES=1−α​σσR​λk\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{ES}}=1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k}. The two iterations are structurally identical, with the correspondence β↔α​σσR\beta\leftrightarrow\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}, up to the additive noise ηt\eta_{t} in the ES case. This yields three key differences:

  1. 1.

    Effective learning rate. The ES effective learning rate α​σσR\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}} is self-normalized by the reward standard deviation σR\sigma_{R}, which depends on the current iterate through ‖𝐯‖2=‖Q​θt‖2\|\mathbf{v}\|^{2}=\|Q\theta_{t}\|^{2} (in the non-simplified version). In contrast, the GD learning rate β\beta is a fixed hyperparameter. This self-normalization provides ES with a degree of automatic step-size adaptation absent in vanilla GD.

  2. 2.

    Stability threshold. GD diverges when λk>2/β\lambda_{k}>2/\beta; ES diverges when λk>2​σR/(α​σ)\lambda_{k}>2\sigma_{R}/(\alpha\sigma). The ES threshold is typically more permissive since σR≥σξ\sigma_{R}\geq\sigma_{\xi} inflates the denominator, though this comes at the cost of a smaller effective step size.

  3. 3.

    Asymptotic behavior. GD converges to θ∗=0\theta^{*}=0 exactly along stable directions, with zero residual error. ES converges only in distribution, with asymptotic variance α2N⁡(1−(γkES)2)\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N(1-(\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{ES}})^{2})} per direction — a noise floor set by the exploration–exploitation tradeoff that cannot be eliminated without increasing NN. On flat directions (λk=0\lambda_{k}=0), GD stays frozen at the initial value, while ES undergoes unbounded diffusion with variance growing as α2​tN\frac{\alpha^{2}t}{N}.

These comparisons are summarized by:

Gradient DescentEvolution StrategyEff. learning rateβα​σ/σRContraction factor ​γk1−β​λk1−α​σσR​λkStability boundλk<2/βλk<2​σR/(α​σ)Optimal curvatureλk=1/βλk=σR/(α​σ)Residual error (stable)0α2N⁡(1−γk2)Flat direction (λk=0)frozendiffusion ∼α2​tN\begin{array}[]{lcc}\hline\cr&\textbf{Gradient Descent}&\textbf{Evolution Strategy}\\ \hline\cr\text{Eff.\ learning rate}&\beta&\alpha\sigma/\sigma_{R}\\ \text{Contraction factor }\gamma_{k}&1-\beta\lambda_{k}&1-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}\lambda_{k}\\ \text{Stability bound}&\lambda_{k}<2/\beta&\lambda_{k}<2\sigma_{R}/(\alpha\sigma)\\ \text{Optimal curvature}&\lambda_{k}=1/\beta&\lambda_{k}=\sigma_{R}/(\alpha\sigma)\\ \text{Residual error (stable)}&0&\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N(1-\gamma_{k}^{2})}\\ \text{Flat direction ($\lambda_{k}=0$)}&\text{frozen}&\text{diffusion }\sim\frac{\alpha^{2}t}{N}\\ \hline\cr\end{array} (139)

E.7 Solution geometry: GD vs. ES on quadratic landscape

We formalize the geometric claims of the main text by comparing the GD and ES solutions after TT steps on the same quadratic landscape R⁡(θ)=−12​θ⊤​Q​θR(\theta)=-\frac{1}{2}\theta^{\top}Q\theta, starting from the same initialization θ0\theta_{0}. Let Q=∑kλk​𝐮k​𝐮k⊤Q=\sum_{k}\lambda_{k}\mathbf{u}_{k}\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top} with λk≥0\lambda_{k}\geq 0.

GD solution

From Section E.6, the GD iterate is deterministic:

θGD:=θTGD=∑k=1d(1−β​λk)T​(𝐮k⊤​θ0)​𝐮k.\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}:=\theta_{T}^{\mathrm{GD}}=\sum_{k=1}^{d}(1-\beta\lambda_{k})^{T}\,(\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{0})\,\mathbf{u}_{k}. (140)

The displacement from initialization is

θGD−θ0=∑k=1d[(1−β​λk)T−1]​(𝐮k⊤​θ0)​𝐮k.\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}-\theta_{0}=\sum_{k=1}^{d}\bigl[(1-\beta\lambda_{k})^{T}-1\bigr](\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{0})\,\mathbf{u}_{k}. (141)

Crucially, directions with λk=0\lambda_{k}=0 contribute nothing: (1−β⋅0)T−1=0(1-\beta\cdot 0)^{T}-1=0. Thus θGD−θ0\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}-\theta_{0} lies entirely within the column space of QQ (the “task-relevant” subspace). If QQ has rank r≪dr\ll d, the GD displacement is confined to an rr-dimensional subspace, regardless of the number of steps TT.

The squared displacement along each active direction is

|𝐮k⊤​(θGD−θ0)|2=[1−(1−β​λk)T]2​(𝐮k⊤​θ0)2,|\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}(\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}-\theta_{0})|^{2}=\bigl[1-(1-\beta\lambda_{k})^{T}\bigr]^{2}\,(\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{0})^{2}, (142)

and for converged directions (|γkGD|≪1|\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{GD}}|\ll 1, large TT) this saturates to (𝐮k⊤​θ0)2(\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{0})^{2}, i.e., the iterate reaches the optimum 𝐮k⊤​θ∗=0\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta^{*}=0.

ES solution

From Section E.5, the simplified ES iterate is

θES:=θTES=HEST​θ0+∑t=1THESt−1​ηT−t,\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}:=\theta_{T}^{\mathrm{ES}}=H_{\mathrm{ES}}^{T}\,\theta_{0}+\sum_{t=1}^{T}H_{\mathrm{ES}}^{t-1}\,\eta_{T-t}, (143)

with HES=I−α​σσR​QH_{\mathrm{ES}}=I-\frac{\alpha\sigma}{\sigma_{R}}Q and ηt∼𝒩⁡(0,α2N​Id)\eta_{t}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}I_{d}).

The displacement decomposes as

θES−θ0=(HEST−I)​θ0⏟signal (deterministic)+∑t=1THESt−1​ηT−t⏟noise (stochastic).\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{0}=\underbrace{(H_{\mathrm{ES}}^{T}-I)\theta_{0}}_{\text{signal (deterministic)}}+\underbrace{\sum_{t=1}^{T}H_{\mathrm{ES}}^{t-1}\,\eta_{T-t}}_{\text{noise (stochastic)}}. (144)

The signal term has exactly the same structure as the GD displacement, with β↔α​σ/σR\beta\leftrightarrow\alpha\sigma/\sigma_{R}: it lies within the column space of QQ and vanishes on flat directions. The noise term, however, is isotropic in origin — each ηt\eta_{t} is drawn from 𝒩⁡(0,α2N​Id)\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}I_{d}) — and thus has support in all dd dimensions.

Along each eigendirection, the mean and variance of the ES displacement are:

𝔼⁡[𝐮k⊤​(θES−θ0)]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}(\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{0})] =[(γkES)T−1]​𝐮k⊤​θ0,\displaystyle=\bigl[(\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{ES}})^{T}-1\bigr]\,\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{0}, (145)
Var⁡[𝐮k⊤​(θES−θ0)]\displaystyle\mathrm{Var}[\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}(\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{0})] =α2N⋅{1−(γkES)2​T1−(γkES)2,(γkES)2≠1,T,(γkES)2=1.\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}\cdot\begin{cases}\dfrac{1-(\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{ES}})^{2T}}{1-(\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{ES}})^{2}},&(\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{ES}})^{2}\neq 1,\\[6.0pt] T,&(\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{ES}})^{2}=1.\end{cases} (146)

For flat directions (λk=0\lambda_{k}=0, γkES=1\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{ES}}=1), the mean displacement is zero but the variance grows as α2​TN\frac{\alpha^{2}T}{N} — a random walk. For active directions (λk>0\lambda_{k}>0, |γkES|<1|\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{ES}}|<1), the mean displacement converges to −𝐮k⊤​θ0-\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{0} (same target as GD) while the variance saturates to α2N⁡(1−(γkES)2)\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N(1-(\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{ES}})^{2})}.

Decomposition of squared displacements

The total expected squared displacement of ES from initialization decomposes as

𝔼​‖θES−θ0‖2\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\|\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{0}\|^{2} =∑k:λk>0([1−(γkES)T]2(𝐮k⊤θ0)2+α2N⋅1−(γkES)2​T1−(γkES)2)\displaystyle=\sum_{k:\,\lambda_{k}>0}\Bigl(\bigl[1-(\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{ES}})^{T}\bigr]^{2}(\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\top}\theta_{0})^{2}+\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N}\cdot\frac{1-(\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{ES}})^{2T}}{1-(\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{ES}})^{2}}\Bigr)
+∑k:λk=0α2​TN.\displaystyle\quad+\sum_{k:\,\lambda_{k}=0}\frac{\alpha^{2}T}{N}. (147)

The first sum runs over the rr active directions and contains both signal and noise; the second sum runs over the d−rd-r flat directions and is pure noise. For r≪dr\ll d (low-rank task structure), the flat-direction contribution dominates:

𝔼​‖θES−θ0‖2≈‖θGD−θ0‖2⏟𝒪⁡(r)+α2​T​dN⏟off-manifold diffusion, ​𝒪​(d).\mathbb{E}\|\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{0}\|^{2}\approx\underbrace{\|\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}-\theta_{0}\|^{2}}_{\mathcal{O}(r)}+\underbrace{\frac{\alpha^{2}Td}{N}}_{\text{off-manifold diffusion, }\mathcal{O}(d)}. (148)

By contrast, GD has ‖θGD−θ0‖2=𝒪⁡(r)\|\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}-\theta_{0}\|^{2}=\mathcal{O}(r) with no off-manifold contribution.

Geometry of θES−θGD\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}

The difference between the two solutions is

θES−θGD=(HEST−HGDT)​θ0⏟signal mismatch+∑t=1THESt−1​ηT−t⏟ES noise.\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}=\underbrace{(H_{\mathrm{ES}}^{T}-H_{\mathrm{GD}}^{T})\theta_{0}}_{\text{signal mismatch}}+\underbrace{\sum_{t=1}^{T}H_{\mathrm{ES}}^{t-1}\,\eta_{T-t}}_{\text{ES noise}}. (149)

The signal mismatch term lies within the column space of QQ and reflects the difference in effective learning rates (α​σ/σR\alpha\sigma/\sigma_{R} vs. β\beta). For converged directions where both methods have reached the optimum, this term vanishes: (γkES)T≈(γkGD)T≈0(\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{ES}})^{T}\approx(\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{GD}})^{T}\approx 0. The noise term is identical to the ES noise analyzed above.

Thus, in the large-TT regime where both methods have converged on the active directions:

𝔼​‖θES−θGD‖2\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\|\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}\|^{2} ≈∑k:λk>0α2N⁡(1−(γkES)2)+∑k:λk=0α2​TN\displaystyle\approx\sum_{k:\,\lambda_{k}>0}\frac{\alpha^{2}}{N(1-(\gamma_{k}^{\mathrm{ES}})^{2})}+\sum_{k:\,\lambda_{k}=0}\frac{\alpha^{2}T}{N}
≈α2​T​(d−r)N+𝒪⁡(r),\displaystyle\approx\frac{\alpha^{2}T(d-r)}{N}+\mathcal{O}(r), (150)

which is dominated by the off-manifold random walk for r≪dr\ll d.

Summary of geometric structure

The three pairwise distances satisfy the approximate hierarchy (for r≪dr\ll d, large TT):

‖θGD−θ0‖2\displaystyle\|\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}-\theta_{0}\|^{2} =𝒪⁡(r),\displaystyle=\mathcal{O}(r),
𝔼​‖θES−θ0‖2\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\|\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{0}\|^{2} =𝒪⁡(r)+𝒪⁡(d),\displaystyle=\mathcal{O}(r)+\mathcal{O}(d),
𝔼​‖θES−θGD‖2\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\|\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}\|^{2} =𝒪⁡(d).\displaystyle=\mathcal{O}(d). (151)

The first displacement is low-dimensional and lies within the column space of QQ. The second is the sum of a comparable on-manifold component and a much larger isotropic off-manifold diffusion. The third is dominated by the off-manifold component alone, since both methods converge to the same optimum within the active subspace. This triangle of displacements accounts for the empirical observation that θES\theta_{\mathrm{ES}} achieves similar task performance to θGD\theta_{\mathrm{GD}} (shared on-manifold component) while being far from it in parameter space (off-manifold diffusion).

Remark 10 (Cosine similarity).

The cosine similarity between the two displacement vectors is

cos⁡∠⁡(θES−θ0,θGD−θ0)=(θES−θ0)⊤​(θGD−θ0)‖θES−θ0‖​‖θGD−θ0‖.\cos\angle(\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{0},\;\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}-\theta_{0})=\frac{(\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{0})^{\top}(\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}-\theta_{0})}{\|\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{0}\|\,\|\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}-\theta_{0}\|}. (152)

Since θGD−θ0\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}-\theta_{0} lies within the column space of QQ and the ES noise is zero-mean, the expected inner product picks up only the on-manifold signal of ES:

𝔼⁡[(θES−θ0)⊤​(θGD−θ0)]=(θGD′−θ0)⊤​(θGD−θ0),\mathbb{E}[(\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{0})^{\top}(\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}-\theta_{0})]=(\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}^{\prime}-\theta_{0})^{\top}(\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}-\theta_{0}), (153)

where θGD′\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}^{\prime} denotes GD with learning rate α​σ/σR\alpha\sigma/\sigma_{R} instead of β\beta. For large TT with both converged on active directions, this approaches ‖θGD−θ0‖2=𝒪⁡(r)\|\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}-\theta_{0}\|^{2}=\mathcal{O}(r). Meanwhile, ‖θES−θ0‖=𝒪⁡(d)\|\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{0}\|=\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{d}), so

𝔼⁡[cos⁡∠⁡(θES−θ0,θGD−θ0)]∼𝒪⁡(r/d),\mathbb{E}\left[\cos\angle(\theta_{\mathrm{ES}}-\theta_{0},\;\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}-\theta_{0})\right]\sim\mathcal{O}\!\left(\sqrt{r/d}\right), (154)

which is small for r≪dr\ll d: the two displacement vectors are nearly orthogonal despite leading to similar task performance.
